packet.title: Full UCA collations (implementation, two packets)
packet.summary: Implements the full Unicode Collation Algorithm over a read at first use from data the host serves, with every UCA parameter and CLDR tailorings for lang and reorder.

item.p: Specifications: F&O 4.0, 5.2.4 "The Unicode Collation Algorithm" (the URI parameters fallback, lang, version, strength, maxVariable, alternate, backwards, normalization, caseLevel, caseFirst, numeric, reorder; FOCH0002); UTS #10 (UCA, version 16.0, matching sxml's Unicode 16.0.0 tables) with its DUCET; UTS #35, Part 5 (CLDR collation: the root collation, tailoring rule syntax, the case and numeric options).
Unlocks:
QT4 advanced-uca-fallback 49 (fn-compare, fn-contains, fn-starts-with, fn-substring-after and others);
non_unicode_codepoint_collation 13 XQ40 / 5 XP40;
the 4 XQST0038 failures;
XSLT sorts with lang;
for the unit tests, Unicode's CollationTest files (owner question 4).
Replaces: in src/collation.c, the UCA fallback and the FOCH0002 of fallback=no; the driver's advanced-uca-fallback.
7.15a DUCET and the algorithm:
a collation element table (glossary ) generated from allkeys.txt by tools/generate-unicode-tables.py, with implicit weights for Han and unassigned code points computed, not stored;
contractions and expansions, variable weighting, and the parameters strength, alternate, maxVariable, backwards, caseLevel, caseFirst, numeric and normalization;
the existing sort-key form (fn:collation-key) and substring matching by collation units (F&O 4.0, 5.2) over the new elements;
the fallback becomes the table's behaviour.

Done 2026-10-19 (): the table is read at first use from the DUCET the host serves (option 4; no generated tables, so tools/generate-unicode-tables.py is unchanged); QT4 advanced-uca-fallback 49 of 49 and non_unicode_codepoint_collation 13 of 13 (XQ40) and 5 of 5 (XP40), the XQST0038 cases pass; CollationTest samples (non-ignorable and shifted) pass in tests/collation_uca_test.c. The gate is met. Left for 7.15b: tailorings (lang, reorder) and the XSLT driver serving the DUCET.

7.15b Tailoring: lang and reorder through CLDR rules compiled at first use into a tailoring (glossary ). The rules are a built-in set for a few languages, or come through the resolver (option 4). Owner question 5 names the set.

Done 2026-10-19 (): option 4 over one resource kind (COLLATION_DATA with urn:sxml:collation-data: + a CLDR path, no COLLATION_TAILORING kind): the CLDR root (allkeys_CLDR.txt) and the LDML files of en, de, fr, it, es, nl and their regions (CLDR 47, third_party/cldr), compiled at first use by src/collation_tailoring.c; reorder over the groups of the generated src/collation_tables.c (tools/generate-collation-tables.py; the DUCET part of tools/generate-unicode-tables.py stays unused). The QT4 and XSLT drivers and the sxml command serve the data; xsl:sort lang works. No QT4 or XT40 case lost. Left: [before n], special reset positions, prefixes and [suppressContractions] (root's search, eor and emoji types), the JavaScript package's data.
Header: none (the collation URIs are already public). With option 4, processor.h gets the resource kinds COLLATION_DATA and COLLATION_TAILORING.
After: 7.2; 7.15b after 7.15a.
Owns: src/collation.c, src/collation_internal.h, new src/collation_uca.c, src/collation_tailoring.c and src/collation_tables.c (generated), and tools/generate-unicode-tables.py (the DUCET part).
Size: 170–280 KB with built-in tables; about 15 KB of code with option 4.
Gate: ≥ 95 % of the 49 and ≥ 90 % of the others; CollationTest (non-ignorable and shifted) passes in a unit test.
